bugs.error_message: DeliveryConnection.settings.default_parcel_stock was confirmed (via tinker) saved as the string "0", yet Ozon rejected every parcel with "Products data required for stock parcels" — the error Ozon gives specifically for a STOCK parcel (parcel-stock=1) missing product data.
bugs.root_cause: Investigated the full chain (OzonShipmentService::send() -> resolveParcelStock() -> OzonExpressConnector::createShipment()'s array_filter) end-to-end, including a settings-cast round-trip test — the PREVIOUS session's resolveParcelStock() (`$options['parcel_stock'] ?? null` + `!== null && !== ''`) already correctly preserved an EXPLICIT "0" through to the payload; that specific reported mechanism could not be reproduced. The REAL gap: (1) the connector's own fallback, used whenever nothing is configured, was "1" (a stock parcel) — for any merchant who never explicitly set default_parcel_stock, every send defaulted into stock-parcel mode; (2) `products` was NEVER built or sent from order line items anywhere in the codebase — OzonShipmentService::send() had no products-building logic at all — so a stock parcel (whether via the "1" default or an explicit "1") was GUARANTEED to fail with exactly this error, every time, for every store.
bugs.fix: Moved the authoritative parcel-stock resolution to `OzonShipmentService::resolveParcelStock(array $settings): string` (public static, directly testable) using `array_key_exists('default_parcel_stock', $settings)` — never `??`/`?:`/`empty()`, all of which treat "0" as absent — defaulting to "0" (not "1") when the key is missing OR explicitly empty. The connector's own `normalizeParcelStock()` is now only a last-resort '0' guard, never inventing '1'. Added `buildProductsPayload()` (reuses the existing, already-tested `OrderLineItems::for()` — read-only, no inventory logic touched) to build `[{ref, qty}]` from order line SKUs; `validateReadiness()` now blocks BEFORE calling Ozon when the resolved stock mode is "1" and no product SKUs exist ("Ozon stock parcels require product details."); products are sent whenever available regardless of stock mode, per Ozon's own docs listing them as generally-helpful/optional. `debugInfo()`/`logCreateShipmentIssue()` now receive the actual outgoing payload and report parcel_stock_sent/parcel_price_sent/parcel_city_sent/has_products/products_count/provider_message — makes "what did we actually send" verifiable without guessing, which is what this investigation needed and didn't have last time.

bugs.error_message: "Send to Ozon" failed with a real Ozon response: HTTP 200, {"ADD-PARCEL": {"CUSTOMER": {"RESULT": "SUCCESS", ...}, "RESULT": "ERROR", "MESSAGE": "Price without commas"}} — but the app still showed the generic "Ozon did not return a tracking number."
bugs.root_cause: TWO separate gaps: (1) parcel-price was sent as whatever `cod_amount` happened to be (a raw float or string) with no normalization at all — the reporter traced it to locale-formatted display values (e.g. the JS `fmtMoney()` helper's `toLocaleString(undefined, ...)`, which renders a comma decimal separator under a French/Moroccan browser locale) leaking into the value used for the API call; Ozon rejects any comma in parcel-price outright. (2) createShipment() decided success/failure purely from HTTP status + "did a tracking number key exist" — it never inspected Ozon's own embedded RESULT/MESSAGE business-error fields, so a 200-with-embedded-error response fell straight through to the generic missing-tracking-number message instead of surfacing Ozon's actual, specific complaint.
bugs.fix: Added `OzonExpressConnector::formatParcelPrice()` (public static, directly unit-testable): accepts int/float/any reasonably-shaped string, strips currency labels and all whitespace (incl. non-breaking space), detects which of comma/dot is the DECIMAL separator by whichever appears LAST in the string (the other is treated as a thousands separator and stripped), then rounds to the nearest whole MAD (PHP's default half-away-from-zero) — matches Ozon's own examples exactly (93.99/"93,99"/"93,99 MAD" all -> "94"). Added extractProviderBusinessError(): checks body['ADD-PARCEL']/['add-parcel']['RESULT'] !== 'SUCCESS' BEFORE falling back to the generic no-tracking-number message, checked in BOTH the HTTP-failed branch and the no-tracking-number branch — HTTP status is never sufficient alone. A tracking number present in the body is still trusted as success on its own, regardless of whether RESULT is explicitly SUCCESS.

bugs.error_message: With city mapping working correctly, "Send to Ozon" still failed every time with the generic "Ozon did not return a tracking number."
bugs.root_cause: TWO compounding gaps: (1) createShipment() only checked TWO tracking-number key variants (TRACKING-NUMBER, tracking_number) via a single generic unwrap() heuristic that only unwraps a body with EXACTLY one top-level key — a real response using any other casing (tracking-number, trackingNumber, TRACKING_NUMBER) or nested under a NAMED wrapper alongside other keys (e.g. {"data": {...}, "success": true}) was never read at all. (2) parcel-stock — REQUIRED by Ozon's docs — was built purely from `$options['parcel_stock'] ?? null`; when a store's Ozon connection had no `default_parcel_stock` configured (the common case — nothing in the UI ever required setting one), array_filter's null-drop silently OMITTED the field from the request entirely, and Ozon likely rejected the parcel for a reason the code never surfaced (the response body reading fell straight through to the generic missing-tracking-number message, since there was no distinct 'response failed to parse or had a provider error message' branch calling out that difference clearly enough).
bugs.fix: Added extractTrackingNumber() checking all 5 documented key casings against 4 candidate locations (bare body, the existing unwrap() result, and explicit data/parcel/add-parcel/ADD-PARCEL wrapper keys). Added resolveParcelStock() so parcel-stock is NEVER omitted — falls back to Ozon's own documented default "1" when neither the request options nor the connection's settings provide one. Added a distinct non-JSON-response branch (checks `is_array($body)` right after decode) so an HTML/plain-text error page from Ozon reports "Ozon create parcel returned a non-JSON response." instead of the misleading tracking-number message. extractError() now also checks MESSAGE/Message/ERROR-MESSAGE casings and is only used as the error text when a real provider message exists — the generic missing-tracking-number message is now the true last resort, never the first thing shown.

bugs.error_message: "Béni Mellal" was already mapped to Ozon city "Beni Mellal" in the City mapping UI, but clicking "Send to Ozon" on an order whose city showed as "beni mellal" still returned "This city is not mapped to an Ozon city. Please map it first."
bugs.root_cause: OzonShipmentService::mappingFor() looked up CityDeliveryProviderMapping ONLY by $order->shipping_city_id (the internal City FK) — and returned null immediately (never even querying) whenever that column was null. But the Confirmation Desk does not require every order to be confirmed against a picked internal city (an agent can confirm without explicitly selecting one, and OrderAddressSummary::matchCity() — the auto-match used during confirmation — only does an EXACT case-sensitive name comparison, so an accented internal name like "Béni Mellal" never auto-matches a plain-ASCII platform string like "beni mellal" in the first place). The order's only city information was therefore the raw platform text sitting in platform_data, which the lookup never consulted at all — a real, correctly-saved mapping was simply never reachable from send-to-Ozon.
bugs.fix: Replaced the single shipping_city_id-only lookup with DeliveryCityMappingResolver, which tries (1) shipping_city_id's own mapping, (2) the raw platform city text (OrderAddressSummary::extract()['city']) normalized (accent/case/punctuation-stripped via the same App\Support\Delivery\CityNameNormalizer used by the Sync Cities suggestion UI) and matched against the internal city list, (3) the same small alias dictionary (Casa/Casablanca etc.), (4) a direct Ozon-city-name match as a last resort. Every DeliveryCityMappingSuggestionService alias/normalization logic was extracted into the shared CityNameNormalizer so the two can never drift apart — a city the Sync Cities UI calls "matched" now always resolves at send time too.

bugs.error_message: Sync cities still imported 0 Ozon cities even after fixing the base-URL bug — the real https://api.ozonexpress.ma/cities response is {"CITIES": {"37": {"ID":37,"NAME":"Agadir",...}, "49": {...}}}, an OBJECT keyed by city id, not any of the shapes the parser recognized (bare list / {cities:[...]} / {data:[...]}).
bugs.root_cause: listCities()'s shape-detection chain only checked lowercase 'cities' and 'data' keys, falling back to treating the body as a bare list. Ozon's real payload wraps rows in an UPPERCASE 'CITIES' key, and that key's VALUE is itself a JSON object (`{"37": {...}, "49": {...}}`) rather than a JSON array — json_decode(..., true) turns that into a PHP associative array keyed by "37"/"49"/etc, which array_is_list() correctly reports as NOT a list, so the old bare-list fallback never matched it either. Every row was silently dropped.
bugs.fix: Extracted shape detection into extractCityRows(): checks 'CITIES' (uppercase, array_values() to flatten the id-keyed object into a plain list) FIRST, then 'cities', then 'data', then a bare list as before. The id/name extraction already handled ID/NAME casing from the previous fix, so no change needed there — only the outer wrapper detection was missing this specific real-world shape. Also captured REF/DELIVERED-PRICE/RETURNED-PRICE/REFUSED-PRICE per row into new nullable delivery_provider_cities columns (city_ref/delivered_price/returned_price/refused_price).

bugs.error_message: N/A — discovered proactively: the user's IDE had database/migrations/2026_08_24_205731_add_city_sync_fields_to_delivery_connections_table.php open, a file this session never created.
bugs.root_cause: An earlier session edited the delivery_connections CREATE migration in place to add last_city_sync_* columns (safe ONLY if that migration had never been run against a real database). It turned out the user's real dev DB had already run it — so the in-place edit was invisible there, and the user's own tooling generated a defensive ALTER migration (Schema::hasColumn guards) to add the missing columns for real. Left as-is, the create-migration's inline columns and the new ALTER migration would both try to add the same columns — harmless on a FRESH db (ALTER's hasColumn guard skips), but misleading/duplicated intent, and the ALTER migration defines last_city_sync_count as NOT NULL default(0) (no ->nullable()), which the create-migration's version didn't match.
bugs.fix: Reverted the create migration back to NOT including the last_city_sync_* columns, leaving the user's new ALTER migration (2026_08_24_205731_...) as the sole, authoritative source for them — matches how the columns actually came to exist on the real dev DB. Adjusted application/test code to never write NULL to last_city_sync_count (it's NOT NULL default 0 per the real migration) — "never synced" is expressed via last_city_sync_at being null, not via the count.

bugs.error_message: A failed "Sync cities" click left DeliveryConnection with status='disabled', last_error='No Ozon cities were imported. Check the provider response.', while last_tested_at still showed an old successful test — a city-sync problem was disabling the whole (working) authenticated connection.
bugs.root_cause: Two things stacked: (1) syncCities() wrote its failure message into the SAME `last_error` column that test() uses for authentication failures — there was only ever one error field, so a city-sync problem looked identical to an auth problem. (2) storeOzon() force-set `'status' => STATUS_DISABLED` on EVERY save via updateOrCreate, including edits to an already-connected connection (e.g. changing a setting) — so an earlier successful test() (status=connected) got silently reset to disabled the next time the form was submitted, for any reason. Neither of these was syncCities() itself setting status — it never touched that column — but the combination reproduced exactly the reported symptom.
bugs.fix: Added last_city_sync_at/last_city_sync_error/last_city_sync_count as real columns (edited the still-uncommitted create migration directly per this project's one-migration-per-table convention, rather than adding an ALTER) — a completely separate lifecycle from status/last_error. syncCities() now only ever writes to the last_city_sync_* fields. Removed the unconditional `status => disabled` from storeOzon() entirely: a brand-new row gets the column's own default, and updating an existing connection leaves status untouched. Added a proper disconnect() action as the only remaining way to manually set status to disabled.

bugs.error_message: Clicking "Sync cities" on the Ozon connection page always showed a generic "Done." toast, but DeliveryProviderCity::where('provider_code','ozon')->count() stayed 0 — no Ozon cities were ever actually imported, and no error was ever visible either way.
bugs.root_cause: TWO independent bugs stacked on top of each other: (1) OzonExpressConnector::listCities() (and testConnection()) called `/cities` through the customer-scoped client (`$this->client()`), which bases every OTHER Ozon endpoint at `https://api.ozonexpress.ma/customers/{customer_id}/{api_key}/...` — but per Ozon's docs, `/cities` is a plain TOP-LEVEL route (`https://api.ozonexpress.ma/cities`), not nested under the customer path, so every real request 404'd and listCities() always returned an empty list. (2) Independently, DeliveryConnectionController@syncCities (and @test) returned a Laravel `RedirectResponse` (`back()->with(...)`), but the frontend's `run()` helper in Connections.jsx calls it via plain `axios.post()` and reads `res.data.message` directly — axios follows the 302 redirect and resolves with the redirected PAGE'S HTML as `res.data`, so `res.data?.message` was always undefined and the UI fell back to its hardcoded 'Done.' string on EVERY outcome, success or failure alike, completely hiding the real result (this is why the zero-import bug went unnoticed — the UI could never have shown the real error even if bug #1 were the only problem).
bugs.fix: Added a separate `citiesClient()` on the connector that bases at the bare host (no customer/key segment) for `/cities` only; every other endpoint (add-parcel, tracking, delivery-note routes) is untouched, still customer-scoped, per the docs. Changed `syncCities()` to return a real `JsonResponse` with `{ok, message, imported_count, updated_count, total_count}` instead of a redirect, matching the proven JSON pattern already used by ConnectionProfileController's identical axios-driven buttons. Widened the city-row parser to also accept plain `ID`/`NAME` keys (previously only `CITY_ID`/`id`/`city_id` and `CITY_NAME`/`name`/`city_name`). Zero cities imported (whether from an empty response or an unparseable shape) now returns ok:false with the literal message "No Ozon cities were imported. Check the provider response." and writes it to `DeliveryConnection.last_error`; a connector-level failure does the same. Fixed the frontend's post-sync `router.reload()` to include `ozon_cities` in its `only` list (it was missing, so even a successful sync left the city-mapping dropdown showing the stale list).

bugs.error_message: php artisan test --filter=OzonDeliveryNoteTest produced ZERO output (no JSON, no stdout/stderr, exit code 2) instead of a normal pass/fail report — every other new Delivery test file worked fine.
bugs.root_cause: app/Http/Controllers/Controller.php uses the `AuthorizesRequests` trait, which already declares a public `authorize($ability, $arguments)` method. DeliveryNoteController redeclared a private `authorize(Request, DeliveryNote): Store` helper with the same name — an incompatible method-visibility redeclaration, which is a PHP FATAL COMPILE ERROR the moment the class is autoloaded. Because PHP classes are only autoloaded on first reference (not when routes/dashboard.php merely does `[DeliveryNoteController::class, 'create']`), the fatal only fired when a test actually hit one of that controller's routes — which only OzonDeliveryNoteTest did, so only that file crashed the whole PHP process with no catchable output.
bugs.fix: Renamed the private helper to `authorizeStore()`. General rule: never name a private/protected controller helper `authorize` in a controller extending the base Controller (or any class using AuthorizesRequests) — always name-check helper methods against inherited trait methods first when a whole-process crash produces no error output at all.

bugs.error_message: SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 19 NOT NULL constraint failed: delivery_note_shipments.id when adding shipments to a delivery note.
bugs.root_cause: DeliveryNote::shipments() is a belongsToMany over the `delivery_note_shipments` pivot table, which — like every table in this project — uses a ULID primary key (`HasUlids` on the DeliveryNoteShipment model). Calling `$note->shipments()->syncWithoutDetaching([$shipment->id])` inserts a raw pivot row directly via query builder and never instantiates a DeliveryNoteShipment model, so HasUlids' `creating()` hook never fires and `id` is left null, violating the NOT NULL primary key.
bugs.fix: Replaced the sync() call with `DeliveryNoteShipment::firstOrCreate(['delivery_note_id' => ..., 'shipment_id' => ...])`, which goes through normal Eloquent model creation and gets its ULID assigned correctly. General rule in this codebase: never use sync()/syncWithoutDetaching()/attach() on a belongsToMany whose pivot table has its own ULID primary key (rather than a plain composite key) — create the pivot model directly instead.

bugs.error_message: ~15 pre-existing tests (DepartmentDashboardTest, OrderDepartmentsTest) started failing with 'Some lines are not linked to local inventory.' ValidationException as soon as the new O4 unmapped-line confirmation-block check was added — even though their order items carried a real local product_id ULID that should have mapped fine.
bugs.root_cause: OrderLineItems::localProductMap()'s FIRST (direct-ULID) match block used an ARROW function: ->each(fn (Product $product) => $map[(string) $product->id] = $product->id). PHP arrow functions capture enclosing-scope variables BY VALUE automatically, so the assignment inside the arrow function wrote to a throwaway copy of $map, never the real outer $map the method returns. Every OTHER block in the same file already used the correct `function (...) use (&$map): void { ... }` form, which is why only this exact path (a bare local product ULID with no platform_connection_id involvement) was silently broken. This bug pre-dated this session entirely — it was just never exposed because nothing had ever asserted the map actually succeeded for this path; silently resolving to null just meant 'no stock movement', which nobody was checking for.
bugs.fix: Changed the arrow function to a regular closure with `use (&$map)`, matching every other block in the file. Verified via targeted debug dump (OrderLineItems::for($order) returning product_id: null for a real local ULID) before and after the fix.

bugs.error_message: New per-variant stock props (stock_on_hand etc.) set in ProductController@edit were confirmed present via Log::debug immediately after being set, but never appeared in the actual Inertia response/test assertions — 'Undefined array key stock_on_hand'.
bugs.root_cause: Inertia::render('...', ['product' => $product, 'readiness' => $readiness->check($product)]) evaluates array values left-to-right; 'product' => $product stores an OBJECT REFERENCE. $readiness->check($product) (evaluated as the LAST array value) internally calls ProductOptionSnapshot::build($product), which does $product->load(['variants.attributeValues' => ..., 'variants.attributeValues.attribute']) — this REPLACES the `variants` relation with a freshly-queried collection of brand new ProductVariant instances. The stock props were set (via $product->variants->each(...)) on the OLD variant instances BEFORE this line, so they were silently discarded when 'variants' got swapped out from under the same $product object.
bugs.fix: Compute $readinessCheck = $readiness->check($product); as its own statement BEFORE the variant-mutation block (which sets stock_on_hand/options/etc. on each variant), then pass the pre-computed $readinessCheck into the Inertia::render() array instead of calling $readiness->check($product) inline as a later array value.

bugs.error_message: Publishing product changes to Shopify updates title/SKU/price, but stock quantity does not change in Shopify. Also: adjusting stock via the SaaS 'Adjust stock' UI silently never reached Shopify at all.
bugs.root_cause: Two compounding issues. (1) Shopify's quantity is never set via a product/variant update payload at all — it lives on InventoryLevel, keyed by inventory_item_id (per-variant, even for a 'simple' product's single default variant) + location_id, requiring a separate POST /inventory_levels/set.json call. Neither the canonical publish payload nor any 'update quantity' attempt on the product parent can ever work. (2) The actually-reachable adjust-stock flow (ProductController::adjustStock(), POST /dashboard/products/{product}/stock) had the platform HARDCODED to 'woocommerce' only when calling ProductPushService::pushStock()/pushVariantStock() — Shopify was never called from that endpoint at all, so even the pre-existing (partially correct) ProductPushService::shopifyVariantStock()/ShopifyConnector::pushStock() code was dead from the UI's perspective. What existed also re-fetched inventory_item_id and /locations.json (blindly taking index 0) on every single call, with nothing ever caching either.
bugs.fix: ProductController::adjustStock() now pushes to BOTH 'woocommerce' and 'shopify' explicitly (YouCan untouched, keeps its own async path) — local inventory always commits first via InventoryEngine, platform pushes happen strictly after and never roll back on failure. ProductPushService::shopifyVariantStock() rewritten + new shopifySimpleStock() added: both resolve inventory_item_id from CACHED listing data first (ProductVariantChannelListing.external_inventory_item_id / ProductChannelListing.metadata.default_inventory_item_id), fetching+persisting via new ShopifyConnector::getVariantInventoryItemId()/getDefaultVariantInventoryItemId() only when missing. New ShopifyConnector::resolveLocationId() checks PlatformConnection.metadata.location_id first, otherwise fetches /locations.json (prefers active:true), and persists the choice for every future push. New ShopifyConnector::setInventoryLevel() is the only thing that actually changes Shopify stock (POST /inventory_levels/set.json, absolute available). No location resolvable -> exact message 'No Shopify location found for inventory sync.'. ProductChannelPublisher::publishShopify() now also captures inventory_item_id for FREE from the publish response (Shopify already returns it on every variant object) and persists it, so the first stock adjustment after a publish needs no extra fetch — but publish itself still never pushes quantity. Confirmed the canonical mapper never sent inventory_quantity/old_inventory_quantity in the first place; only the legacy console-command-only ShopifyConnector::createVariableProduct()/createVariant() still do (unreachable from the UI, left as a known limitation).

bugs.error_message: Publishing a SaaS product to Shopify updates the title successfully, but the SKU never changes in Shopify, for simple (non-variable) products.
bugs.root_cause: Shopify SKU lives on the variant, not the product parent, even for a 'simple' product (which still has exactly one default variant under the hood). ProductChannelPublisher::publishShopify()'s UPDATE path for a simple product sent the parent PUT with an id-less variants:[{sku,price}] array embedded (from ShopifyProductPayloadMapper::simplePayload()). Without an id, Shopify cannot tell 'update the existing default variant' from 'create a second one', so the sku the user actually sees never changed. This was made worse by a previous session deleting ShopifyConnector::updateVariantPayload() as apparently-dead code once the variable-product path stopped needing per-variant HTTP calls — simple products still needed that exact primitive.
bugs.fix: Simple-product UPDATE now strips variants from the parent payload entirely (mirrors the existing unset() for variable products) and issues an explicit PUT /variants/{id}.json afterward. The default variant id is resolved in priority order: ProductChannelListing.metadata['default_variant_id'] -> the parent response's variants[0].id (already returned by updateProductPayload(), no extra call) -> a new ShopifyConnector::getDefaultVariantId() GET fallback (never throws, returns null on failure). Whichever id is resolved is saved back into metadata for future publishes. CREATE still embeds the variant in the initial payload (correct for a brand-new product) but now verifies the returned sku actually matches before reporting success. Re-added ShopifyConnector::updateVariantPayload(). Added ShopifyProductPayloadMapper::defaultVariantPayload() (sku/price/compare_at_price/barcode) as the single source of truth for both the create payload and the explicit update call. When the parent update succeeds but the variant SKU update fails, the result is now status='failed' with the literal message 'Product updated but Shopify default variant SKU update failed.' — never reported as full success — while the ProductChannelListing (whose parent DID update) is still kept, not rolled back.

bugs.error_message: A product previously tested as variable in SaaS/Shopify, then reverted to simple in Shopify and synced back, shows as simple in the Product Edit UI (stock on hand visible) but Publish Readiness still says "Cannot publish to Shopify because one or more variants are missing option values."
bugs.root_cause: Nothing ever archived a product's old canonical ProductAttribute/ProductAttributeValue/ProductVariant rows when it reverted from variable to simple via an external sync — ProductSyncService::saveProduct() correctly flips product.type to 'simple' from the incoming platform data, but never touched the leftover canonical rows. ProductOptionSnapshot::build() (the single place every readiness check and both platform mappers read through) ignored product.type entirely and just read whatever was still marked active, so the stale variable-state data kept feeding readiness/mapper decisions. Separately, ProductController@update's variable->simple branch only raw-deleted ProductVariant rows, never the ProductAttribute/ProductAttributeValue rows, so switching to simple via the SaaS edit form had the same leak. A secondary bug: an attribute with zero active values (a fully-retired option not yet garbage-collected) still appeared in the snapshot as a phantom {name, values:[]} entry.
bugs.fix: product.type is now authoritative everywhere: ProductOptionSnapshot::build() short-circuits to empty options/variants when !$product->isVariable(), and filters out zero-active-value attributes. ProductPublishReadinessService::shopify() and ShopifyProductPayloadMapper::map() got matching explicit type checks (WooCommerce's already had this). New ProductVariantWizardService::archiveAll() (=sync($product,[],[])) is the shared archive primitive — soft-deletes all active variants (never hard-deletes one with a channel listing/inventory link) and retires all active option values — called from ProductController@update's variable->simple branch AND from ProductSyncService::saveProduct() whenever an authoritative pull flips a product from variable to simple. ProductController@edit also force-empties options/variants props for a simple product regardless of DB state. Fixing archiveAll() exposed a pre-existing latent bug (see bug-archived-variant-sku-unique-collision) that had to be fixed too for the round-trip (simple->variable->simple->variable) to work.

bugs.error_message: SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 19 UNIQUE constraint failed: product_variants.product_id, product_variants.sku — thrown when regenerating variants with a SKU that a previously-archived (soft-deleted) variant already occupies
bugs.root_cause: ProductVariantWizardService::sync()'s existing-variant matching only ever queries ACTIVE variants ($product->variants()->with('attributeValues')->get(), soft-deleted excluded by the default scope) — by design, so an archived variant is never silently resurrected by an unrelated combo. But product_variants has a (product_id, sku) unique index that soft-delete does not exempt. So calling sync() again with a sku a trashed row still occupies (e.g. switching simple -> variable -> simple -> variable with the same SKUs, which archiveAll() now makes a realistic path) tried to ProductVariant::create() a duplicate and hit the DB constraint.
bugs.fix: Added a third matching tier in sync()'s per-variant loop: once combo-match and id-match both miss, look up $product->variants()->onlyTrashed()->where('sku', $sku)->first() (using the FINAL computed sku, after auto-generation) and restore() it instead of creating a new row. Bonus: this reuses the original variant id, so any leftover ProductVariantChannelListing from before the archive reconnects automatically instead of orphaning.

bugs.error_message: Publishing a SaaS variable product to Shopify failed with HTTP 422: {"errors":{"base":["Product options must have corresponding variants. Please include variant data with your request."]}}
bugs.root_cause: Two independent causes, both producing an options-without-variants Shopify payload: (1) ProductChannelPublisher::publishShopify() stripped `variants` from the parent update PUT whenever the product was variable, intending a separate per-variant create/update loop afterward — that first (options-only) request already 422s, the later per-variant calls never got a chance to run. (2) ProductPublishReadinessService::shopify() only WARNED (not blocked) when a product had canonical options defined but zero active variants, so ShopifyProductPayloadMapper::map() happily built a payload with `options` set and an empty `variants` array.
bugs.fix: ProductChannelPublisher::publishShopify() now always sends `options` and `variants` together in ONE request (parent create AND update) — the variant array is rebuilt from the canonical snapshot with each already-linked variant's remote id merged in so Shopify updates it in place instead of duplicating it; no more separate per-variant HTTP calls (ShopifyConnector::createVariantPayload()/updateVariantPayload() deleted as now-dead code). Returned variants are matched back to local variants by option1/option2/option3 combination (not SKU, since Shopify doesn't guarantee echoing it back the same way). ProductPublishReadinessService::shopify() moved the 'options but no variants' case from $warnings to $errors (STATUS_BLOCKED), so the mapper refuses to build the invalid payload at all and the publish is blocked before any HTTP call.

bugs.error_message: Shopify connection page showed "Failed — Missing read_products scope" even though product import/sync was actually working
bugs.root_cause: ShopifyAuthService::testConnection() hard-gated the ENTIRE result on `str_contains($token['scope'], 'read_products')` — a check against the OAuth token response's self-reported scope STRING — before ever attempting the real GET /products.json call. If Shopify's client_credentials grant response formats/omits the scope string differently than expected, this false-negatived the whole connection even when the real API call would have succeeded.
bugs.fix: Did not touch ShopifyAuthService (task: don't rewrite Shopify auth architecture; also has its own passing test suite). Added a new, separate ShopifyCapabilityDiagnosticsService + "Run diagnostics" UI/endpoint that determines every READ capability from a real, safe (non-mutating) Shopify Admin API call's actual HTTP status (200/401/403) — never from the scope string. Write capabilities are reported from scopes only (never mutation-tested, per explicit safety requirement) and are surfaced as their own 'configured'/'not_configured' status, never folded into a pass/fail gate. Connection-level status is now 3-way (connected/partially_configured/failed) and is explicitly never 'failed' when products.read passed.

bugs.error_message: Clicking Publish on a product imported from WooCommerce also pushed it to Shopify whenever the store had an active Shopify connection, even though the user never selected Shopify
bugs.root_cause: ProductController::push() (now removed) grabbed every active PlatformConnection for the store (`$store->connections()->where('status','active')->get()`), grouped by platform, and pushed to all of them unconditionally — there was no concept of a user-selected target at all. The Edit page's "Publish to platforms" button called this route with an empty body.
bugs.fix: Replaced push()/`/push` with publish()+bulkPublish() (`/publish`, `/bulk-publish`), both requiring an explicit, validated `connection_ids` array. New App\Services\Sync\ProductPublishService orchestrates: resolves only connections that belong to the product's own store, checks ProductChannelListing per connection (update if linked, skip with `not_linked_to_channel` unless `create_missing_listings` is true), and never touches a platform the caller didn't name. ProductPushService::pushProduct()/createProduct()/createVariableProduct() gained an optional `$connectionIds` param (defaults to null = old behavior, for any other existing caller) so the orchestrator can scope to exact connections instead of "every connection for a platform". Frontend: both Edit.jsx and Index.jsx now open a PublishTargetModal (default selection: none) instead of posting immediately.

bugs.error_message: Shopify integration page could show a green "Synced" badge and a red "Token is missing the read_products scope" error at the same time
bugs.root_cause: Two independent bugs compounded: (1) backend — ShopifyAuthService::requestToken() called markValid() as soon as ANY non-empty scope came back, before testConnection() went on to check for the specific read_products scope or make the real products.json call; those later checks returned ok:false to the caller but never called markFailed() to correct the already-persisted token_status:'valid'. (2) frontend — the verification panel rendered its StatusBadge from the stale page-load `connection.token_status` prop while rendering the error message from a separately-sourced, ephemeral `testResult` state set only by the just-completed axios response; the two had no way to agree with each other.
bugs.fix: Backend: every exit path of testConnection() (domain invalid, credentials rejected/401, empty scope, missing read_products, products-endpoint 403/401/other, and true success) now calls markValid()/markFailed() with the task-specified exact wording, so exactly one final state is ever persisted per test run. Frontend: dropped the separate testResult state entirely; after a test-connection call, the page does `router.reload({only:['connection']})` and the badge+message are both derived from one computed `state` variable (untested/connected/failed) off the freshly-reloaded `connection` prop — structurally impossible to show both at once. Badge label also renamed Synced->Connected/Failed/Untested.

bugs.error_message: Clicking 'Publish to platforms' on a product that IS linked via ProductChannelListing but never had the deprecated Product.external_id column set silently no-ops ("Product is already linked to this channel") instead of pushing the edited fields to WooCommerce/Shopify/YouCan
bugs.root_cause: push() decided create-vs-update per PLATFORM GROUP using the single legacy Product.external_id flag ($product->external_id ? pushProduct() : createProduct()), not the per-connection ProductChannelListing. createProduct() correctly detects an existing listing and skips (by design, that's pushProduct()'s job) but returns success without pushing any field changes — so a product whose only mapping is the modern channel-listing table (the normal state after Option B2's product migration, or any product synced without external_id ever being backfilled) always took the create branch and never actually updated the remote product.
bugs.fix: push() now decides per platform group via $product->listingForConnection()/externalIdForConnection() on that platform's connection (unique per store+platform) instead of the global legacy flag. Discovered while writing WooCommerceOutboundSyncTest's 'publishes product changes using the existing remote product id' test — Http::assertSent() found zero requests because createProduct() had short-circuited.

bugs.error_message: "Something went wrong: Undefined array key \"description\"" flashed on product create/update whenever an optional field (description/category/compare_price/cost/featured_image) is omitted from the request
bugs.root_cause: store()/update() read $validated['description'] etc. directly instead of with a ?? fallback, even though those keys are validated as 'nullable' — Laravel's $request->validate() omits a nullable key entirely from the returned array when it isn't present in the request at all (as opposed to present-but-null). It was latent because Create.jsx/Edit.jsx's useForm() always initializes those fields to '' so the browser always sends them; a minimal API-style POST (e.g. from tests) without those keys hit it immediately.
bugs.fix: Changed every optional field read to '$validated["x"] ?? null' (and the compare_price/cost ternaries to check '($validated["x"] ?? null)' before casting) in both store() and update().

bugs.error_message: TypeError: App\Http\Controllers\Settings\SettingsController::profileRules(): Argument #1 ($userId) must be of type ?int, string given — 500 on PATCH /settings/profile

The bug was latent and never exercised because the old Volt settings pages 500'd earlier (broken <x-pages::settings.layout> component) before validation ever ran — the new SettingsController (Option B1 migration) was the first real caller to pass $user->id (a ULID string) through.
bugs.fix: Widened profileRules()/emailRules() signatures to 'string|int|null $userId = null' in app/Concerns/ProfileValidationRules.php. No caller changes needed.

bugs.error_message: Dashboard stock adjustment for a variable product doesn't let you pick which variant gets the stock; increments land on the parent product row and don't sync to the correct variant in the POS
bugs.root_cause: StockController::adjustStock hardcoded 'variant_id' => null in Stock::firstOrCreate (line 84), so every dashboard adjustment wrote the product-level stock row regardless of variant. index() also sent no variant data to Stock.jsx, and AdjustStockModal only had a single quantity input — the UI could not offer a variant choice. stock_ledger had no variant_id column so history couldn't attribute a change to a variant.
bugs.fix: index() now eager-loads variants with sellable stock_sum (whereHas warehouse.sellable) and presents { type, has_variants, variant_count, variants:[{id,name,sku,stock}] } via paginator->through(). adjustStock() accepts batch payload { reason, notes, adjustments:[{variant_id,quantity_change}] }, validates that variable products target a real owned variant (and simple products carry null), skips zero rows, and writes each delta to the exact (product,variant,warehouse) Stock row + a variant-tagged StockLedger entry (applyAdjustment helper, one DB transaction). Added variant_id to stock_ledger (migration 2026_07_26_000002) + StockLedger fillable/relation. Frontend: rewrote AdjustStockModal.jsx — simple products keep the single input; variable products get a scrollable per-variant list (name/sku, current stock, signed input, live current→new preview, filter box when >6 variants), submit-disabled until a non-zero row exists. Stock.jsx cards + StockMovements.jsx rows show a variants badge. Sync to POS is automatic: both read the same sellable `stocks` rows (POS presentProduct stock_sum), reflected on the POS's next fetch/search (no websocket push).

bugs.error_message: POS: clicking a variable product (with sizes/colors) failed / added it directly with no way to pick the specific variant
bugs.root_cause: presentProduct() only returned id/name/sku/price/images/stock — it never included variants or attributes. Variable products arrived at the React POS looking identical to simple ones, so onAdd(product) added the BASE product row (base price, aggregate variant stock) via useCart, and cart lines were keyed by product_id alone, so a variant could never be distinguished or chosen. adjustInventory() also hardcoded variant_id => null, so even if a variant sold, the wrong (product-level) Stock row was decremented.
bugs.fix: Backend: presentProduct now eager-loads variants.attributeValues + sellable stock_sum and returns { type, has_variants, variant_count, price_from, attributes:[{name,values}], variants:[{id,name,sku,price,stock,image,options}] }. Added variant_id to pos_order_items (migration 2026_07_26_000001), PosOrderItem fillable+relation, CheckoutController validation (items.*.variant_id nullable exists), OrderProcessingService persists variant_id and decrements the matching variant Stock row. Frontend: new VariantModal.jsx (attribute pill selectors, per-combination live stock, out-of-stock disabling relative to other selections, qty stepper), useCart keyed by composite line_id (`${productId}::${variantId}`) with addItem(product,{variant,quantity}); Dashboard opens the modal for has_variants products (adds simple ones directly) and folds the variant label into the receipt line name; ProductCard/CartItem/Cart/CheckoutPreviewModal made variant-aware.

bugs.error_message: SQLSTATE[42000]: 1059 Identifier name 'product_variant_attribute_values_product_variant_id_product_attribute_value_id_unique' is too long — migrate:fresh aborted at pvav; 38 later migrations sat Pending in the real DB and never ran
bugs.root_cause: The original 61-file migration set could not build a fresh MySQL database. 2026_05_25_000003 created product_variant_attribute_values with $table->unique(['product_variant_id','product_attribute_value_id']) — Laravel's auto-generated index name exceeded MySQL's 64-char limit, so migrate:fresh died there and every migration after it (POS, factures, teams, returns, all the ALTERs) never executed. Separately, several ALTER migrations used native ENUM MODIFY guarded only for mysql, and the committed extend_sync_logs_action_enum lacked the sqlite guard (fails on the sqlite test DB).
bugs.fix: Squashed 61 migrations into 34 clean create-table migrations (one per table), each reflecting the FINAL schema with every add/rename/drop/widen folded in. pvav now uses a composite PRIMARY KEY named 'pvav_primary' (product_variant_id, product_attribute_value_id) — it enforces uniqueness on its own, so the over-long unique index is gone. Evolving lists (orders/pos_orders.fulfillment_status, inventory_adjustments.source) are created as their final VARCHAR; sync_logs.action and factures.status are created with their final ENUM value sets; activity_log morph ids are char(26) from the start. FK dependency order preserved via timestamps (only reorder: store_roles before store_members/store_invitations). Data-only migrations dropped (no-ops on a fresh DB). Verified: migrate:fresh builds all 40 tables cleanly on MySQL; Pest suite 189 pass / 7 pre-existing failures (onboarding-redirect + deleted settings.profile component on the cleanup branch, unrelated to schema). Extracted ground truth via a throwaway scratch DB (saas_squash_tmp); the real saas_commerce dev DB was never touched.

bugs.error_message: Synced WooCommerce orders all collapse onto ONE row (new orders take older orders' data); re-sync also resets an order's status back to Pending every minute
bugs.root_cause: 1) WooCommerceConnector::parseOrder returned 'external_id'/'order_number' but BaseConnector::normalizeOrder reads 'platform_id'/'number' with no fallback -> platform_id='' for every WC order. The unique key (platform_connection_id, platform_order_id) then matched the single ('conn','') row, so every order overwrote it (Shopify/YouCan were fine — they emit platform_id). 2) OrderSyncService::saveOrder used updateOrCreate and set status=OrderStatus::Pending in the values on EVERY sync, resetting the commercial status of already-advanced orders and clobbering their volatile fields.
bugs.fix: WooCommerceConnector::parseOrder now emits 'platform_id'/'number'; normalizeOrder falls back to external_id/order_number defensively. saveOrder rewritten: returns ?Order; skips (logs) empty platform_id; looks up existing by (connection,platform_order_id); if it exists and fulfillment_status !== Pending it is left untouched (SaaS owns the lifecycle), if still Pending only volatile platform data is refreshed (never status); new orders are Order::create'd with status=Pending AND fulfillment_status=Pending (awaiting confirmation) then fire OrderCreated + SendWhatsAppConfirmation. syncFromPlatform loop skips null returns. Tests: tests/Feature/Orders/OrderSyncServiceTest.php (6). NOTE: there is NO order webhook — sync is poll-only; both scheduler and SyncPlatformOrders job share this saveOrder path. Existing single empty-platform_order_id row from the old bug can be deleted manually.

bugs.error_message: Scheduled sync failed: OrderSyncService::syncFromPlatform(): Argument #3 ($since) must be of type ?Carbon\Carbon, Carbon\CarbonImmutable given, called in routes/console.php on line 24
bugs.root_cause: AppServiceProvider.php:109 sets Date::use(CarbonImmutable::class) globally, so every model datetime cast and now() returns CarbonImmutable. The scheduler passes $connection->last_synced_at->subMinutes(5) (a CarbonImmutable) into syncFromPlatform(), whose $since param was hinted ?Carbon\Carbon. CarbonImmutable is NOT a subclass of Carbon (both are siblings under CarbonInterface), so the TypeError fired. The connectors' getOrders(?Carbon $since) had the same too-narrow hint downstream.
bugs.fix: Widened $since to ?Carbon\CarbonInterface in OrderSyncService::syncFromPlatform and getOrders across BaseConnector (abstract) + all three connectors (import changed Carbon\Carbon -> Carbon\CarbonInterface; Carbon was used nowhere else in those files). CarbonInterface is the shared parent so it accepts both mutable and immutable. Verified by reflection + full suite (225/183, 7 pre-existing).

bugs.error_message: SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1452 ... stocks_product_id_foreign ... insert into stocks (product_id, ...) values (7778, ...) — confirming an online (WooCommerce) order threw a FK violation
bugs.root_cause: OrderLineItems::fromOnline() copied product_id/variant_id straight from the orders.items JSON blob, but that blob stores the PLATFORM's ids (e.g. WooCommerce product id 7778), not local ULIDs. On confirm, OrderWorkflowService::applyStockEffects() -> StockMovementWriter::move(productId:'7778') tried to firstOrCreate a stocks row whose product_id (7778) has no matching products.id (all ULIDs) -> FK 1452. The class docblock already promised product_id was the LOCAL id (nullable when unmatched); fromOnline violated that. Also latently affected ReturnInspectionService (other OrderLineItems::for consumer).
bugs.fix: fromOnline() now resolves each raw id (platform external_id OR an already-local ULID) to the local product/variant ULID via batched lookups (localProductMap/localVariantMap, scoped to order store_id, matching external_id OR id). Unmatched -> null, so StockMovementWriter::move() skips it (its productId===null guard). POS path (fromPos) unchanged — pos_order_items.product_id is already a local FK. Regression tests added to tests/Feature/Orders/OrderWorkflowServiceTest.php: (1) platform external_id 7778 resolves + deducts stock, (2) unmatched id moves no stock and does not throw.

Suite unchanged (181 pass / 7 pre-existing). bugs.root_cause: The prior ticket's buildProductsPayload() built each product row as {"ref": ..., "qty": N} — but Ozon's own documented add-parcel products schema uses the key "qnty", not "qty". Separately, parcel-open was being treated as a boolean in the UI/settings (checkbox) and forwarded as-is, but Ozon documents parcel-open as "1" (ouvrir le colis) / "2" (ne pas ouvrir) — not a boolean at all; a checked/unchecked value could never map to Ozon's real 1/2 vocabulary.

bugs.error_message: Tailwind v4 custom utility hover selector was initially expressed as @utility btn-primary:hover.
bugs.root_cause: Tailwind's @utility directive defines utility names; pseudo-state selectors must be ordinary CSS selectors rather than utility names containing a colon.
bugs.fix: Changed the hover rules to standard .btn-primary:hover and .card-interactive:hover selectors before verification.

bugs.error_message: apply_patch rejected a patch that deleted and re-added the same path in one operation.
bugs.root_cause: The patch encoded a full-file replacement as simultaneous delete/add directives for one file, which the patch parser treats as an invalid duplicate path operation.
bugs.fix: Applied the replacement as two ordered patch operations and used normal update hunks for subsequent edits.

bugs.error_message: rg reported an invalid file-name syntax for resources/js/Components/PremiumDashboard/*.jsx on Windows.
bugs.root_cause: The wildcard was passed as a path argument in a Windows invocation where ripgrep did not expand the glob.
bugs.fix: Enumerated the directory directly and used ripgrep directory paths or -g filters rather than a shell-expanded path wildcard.

bugs.error_message: Get-Process could not bind the Id argument because the common-port listener probe returned null.
